title.topic:
The Children of Israel—
God Feeding His People
title.point: In the same way that God cared for the Israelites, He takes care of us — He knows what we need before we even ask!

lastWeekReview.title: The Children of Israel—Praising, then Complaining
bullets: After crossing the Red Sea, the Israelites PRAISED God by singing!
Miriam took a tambourine and all the women danced and sang!
But the praising didn't last — they quickly started COMPLAINING!
At Marah, they found bitter water and grumbled to Moses.
God showed Moses a tree — when he threw it in, the bitter water became SWEET!
God still cared for them even when they complained. Let's be praisers, not complainers!
lastWeekReview.discussion: 📖  Did anyone try to turn a complaint into praise this week? How did it feel? Remember — praising makes us happy, and it makes God happy too!
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: "I will praise You… Your works are wonderful, and my soul knows it well." — Psalm 139:14

kidsContent.text: The Israelites were on a long journey through the wilderness, and they got HUNGRY. Instead of trusting God, they started complaining again! They said, 'We had so much food in Egypt — now we're going to die out here!'
But God had a plan! He told Moses, 'I will rain bread from heaven for you.' And sure enough — the next morning, the ground was covered with tiny, white, round flakes!
The Israelites had never seen anything like it. They looked at each other and said, 'Manna?' — which means 'What is it?' And that's how manna got its name!
Moses told them, 'This is the bread which Jehovah has given you to eat.' The Bible says it tasted like wafers made with honey — doesn't that sound delicious?
🌟 Even when the people complained, God still provided! He rained down bread from heaven just for them!

image.caption: Israelites gather manna and quail in the wilderness

kidsContent.text: There were special rules for gathering manna: each person gathered just enough for one day. They couldn't save leftovers! Some people tried anyway — and their leftover manna got WORMS and stank! Yuck!

But on the sixth day, they gathered DOUBLE — enough for two days. Why? Because the seventh day was the Sabbath, a day of rest. No manna would fall that day, but amazingly, the extra manna stayed perfectly fresh!
God didn't just send manna — He also sent QUAIL (small birds like chickens) for meat! And He gave them water too. Every single thing they needed, God provided.
Here's the most amazing part: the Israelites wandered for FORTY YEARS, and their clothes and shoes NEVER wore out! How? Because God was taking care of every detail!
🌟 God knows what we need before we even ask! Instead of complaining, we can trust that He will take care of everything!

image.caption: Happy Israelites gathering manna into baskets

lesson.practicePoint: This week, whenever you need something, try PRAYING first instead of worrying or complaining. Trust that God already knows what you need! Share what happened next week.

memoryVerse.text: …Your Father knows the things that you have need of before you ask Him.
memoryVerse.application: The Israelites were hungry and afraid, but God already had a plan — bread from heaven! Just like He provided manna every single morning, our Heavenly Father knows exactly what we need, even before we ask Him.

parts.text: Materials: Cotton balls (manna), baskets/bags, timer, cards with Bible questions
Setup: Scatter cotton balls ('manna') all over the floor. Each kid gets a small bag or basket.
Round 1 — Daily Portion: Kids have 30 seconds to gather EXACTLY 10 cotton balls (no more, no less!). Too many or too few = try again! Just like the Israelites gathered just enough for one day.
Round 2 — Double Portion: This time, gather EXACTLY 20 — it's the sixth day! Kids who get it right earn a bonus point.
Round 3 — Trust Quiz: After gathering, each kid answers a Bible question about the story. Correct answer = keep your manna. Wrong = put some back!
Discussion: Was it hard to gather the right amount? The Israelites had to trust God to send just enough every day!
📖 Connection: God gave exactly what His people needed — not too much, not too little. He takes care of us the same way!

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: The wilderness. The Israelites are tired and hungry. They look miserable.
The Israelites had been traveling through the wilderness, and their food was running out. Instead of trusting God, they started complaining — AGAIN!
I'm SO hungry! Back in Egypt, we had pots full of meat and all the bread we could eat!
Moses and Aaron brought us out here to STARVE! At least in Egypt we had food!
You're not complaining against us — you're complaining against GOD! And He has heard you!
Moses, tell the people: I will rain BREAD from heaven for them! Each morning they shall gather just enough for one day.
The next morning, the ground is covered with tiny white flakes.
What IS this stuff? I've never seen anything like it!
This is the bread Jehovah has given you! Gather just enough for today — no leftovers!
It tastes like wafers made with HONEY! This is delicious!
One Israelite tries to save extra. The next day...
EWWW! My extra manna is full of WORMS and it STINKS! I should have listened!
On the sixth day, gather DOUBLE — because the seventh day is the Sabbath, a day of rest. No manna will fall that day!
And amazingly, the extra manna on the sixth day stayed perfectly fresh! God provided manna every single morning for FORTY YEARS — and their clothes and shoes never wore out!
God knows what we need before we even ask! Instead of complaining, we can trust that our Heavenly Father will take care of everything!

description.text: Setup: Two teams. Scatter cotton balls at one end of the gym. Each team has a basket at the other end.
Rules: One runner at a time sprints to the manna pile, grabs EXACTLY 3 cotton balls, and runs back to drop them in the team basket.
Twist: If a runner grabs more or fewer than 3, they must run back and fix it! No hoarding — just like the Israelites couldn't keep extra!
Bonus Round: On the 'sixth day' call, runners must grab 6 instead of 3 (double portion)!
📖 Connection: God provided manna every day — the Israelites just had to go out and gather it! God provides for us too, but we need to receive what He gives.
Materials: Cotton balls, two baskets, cones for relay lanes
Setup: One leader throws soft balls or bean bags ('quail') into the air. Kids spread out in the gym.
Rules: When the leader yells 'God sends quail!' and tosses the balls, kids try to catch them. Each catch = 1 point.
Freeze Round: Leader calls 'Sabbath REST!' — everyone must freeze. Anyone who moves does 5 jumping jacks.
Team mode: Split into two groups. One group gathers 'manna' (cotton balls from floor), other catches 'quail' (balls from air). Switch after 3 minutes!
📖 Connection: God sent both manna AND quail — He provided everything His people needed, morning and evening!
Materials: Soft balls or bean bags, cotton balls, timer

description.text: Hide cotton balls ('manna') and small toy birds or feathers ('quail') around the outdoor area before kids arrive.
Teams search for both types of 'food.' Manna = 1 point, Quail = 2 points.
Rule: Each kid can only carry 5 items at a time (daily portion). They must return to 'camp' (base) to drop off before gathering more.
Twist: Leader blows a whistle for 'Sabbath' — everyone must stop gathering and rest for 30 seconds!
Materials: Cotton balls, feathers or small toy birds, baskets, whistle

outdoor.tip: 🍞 Manna appeared every morning — what a picture of God's daily faithfulness! Help kids connect this to their own lives: God provides what they need every single day, just like He did for the Israelites.
